Card rail of ten in the paste; no inline citation links.] [QUERENT] dolphindiana gerald [ANSWER] "Dolphindiana" and its construction foreman, Gerald the Dolphin, refer to a viral satirical hoax and internet meme that took social media by storm in March 2026. The Satirical Story The meme originated from a satirical Facebook post by the page The Dude Humor Report. Styled like an official police report, the joke claimed that a sunburnt Florida man named Ricky Hollowell was discovered soaking wet on the Sanibel Causeway drawing elaborate blueprints in the sand. According to the fictional story, the man claimed he was kidnapped by a pod of dolphins and forced to spend three days 40 feet underwater helping them build a secret submarine civilization. Who is Gerald? In the lore of the meme, Gerald is the dolphin project manager and foreman overseeing the underwater construction. The humor of the viral trend mostly centers around the absurd structural specifications of the city and Gerald's management style: • The Blueprints: The blueprints allegedly included zones for condos, a town square, and a recreation center. • "Gerald Handled That": When the man was asked how he managed to breathe underwater for three days, his response was simply, "Gerald handled that. I didn't ask any questions. You don't question Gerald." • The "Dolphindiana" Bureaucracy: The joke evolved into a broader universe on TikTok and Instagram, with users writing fake "labor manifestos" under the "Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana", posting POV videos acting as Gerald's captured human laborers, or joking about applying to buy real estate from him. The Reality The entire phenomenon is a complete hoax. The Lee County Sheriff's Office in Florida even leaned into the joke at the time, playfully issuing a "debunk" stating that their Underwater Construction Investigation Team had failed to find any evidence of the dolphin condos.
